name: How much contingency should I budget for a luxury remodel in older Los Angeles homes?

mainEntity.name: How much contingency should I set aside for a luxury remodel in an older Los Angeles home with unknown conditions behind the walls?
mainEntity.text: How much contingency should I set aside for a luxury remodel in an older Los Angeles home with unknown conditions behind the walls?

acceptedAnswer.text: Older Los Angeles homes often look straightforward until demolition exposes the real condition of the structure and systems. A contingency budget protects the project from stop-and-start delays when hidden issues appear, such as obsolete wiring, undersized plumbing, water damage, rot, or framing that no longer meets current needs. The exact amount depends on age, scope, and whether the project includes structural work, but luxury remodels should always carry a realistic reserve rather than a token amount. Homeowners should ask for separate allowances for unknown conditions, finish upgrades, and permit-driven changes so the budget does not collapse if surprises appear. A thorough preconstruction inspection, engineering review, and demo phase planning can reduce risk, but they will not eliminate it. The safest approach is to budget conservatively and choose a builder who communicates change orders clearly.
acceptedAnswer.description: A luxury remodel in an older Los Angeles home should include a meaningful contingency because hidden issues are common once walls and floors are opened. Older properties can reveal outdated electrical, plumbing, framing, drainage, termite damage, or seismic weaknesses that were not visible during initial planning.
